item.title: Gunkei Temple, Hitoyoshi — Guide
item.description: In the castle town of Hitoyoshi, deep in the mountains of southern Kumamoto along the Kuma River, Gunkei Temple offers a quiet and historic stop amid the valley’s rich cultural heritage. Hitoyoshi flourished for centuries as the seat of the Sagara clan, who ruled the isolated Kuma region for some 700 years, and the town preserves an unusual concentration of old temples, shrines and cultural sites — including nationally important treasures — reflecting a distinctive local Buddhist and Shinto culture.

item.title: Hitoyoshi & the Kuma River — Guide
item.description: The Kuma River, flowing through the Hitoyoshi valley in southern Kumamoto, is renowned as one of the three fastest-flowing rivers in Japan, making it a superb destination for river activities. Its lively rapids and clear waters, set amid green mountains, are ideal for exhilarating white-water rafting trips in the warmer months, with guided tours suitable for beginners and families as well as thrill-seekers. The river is also famous for its traditional ‘kudari’ boat descents, in which passengers ride wooden boats steered by skilled boatmen down the current through the scenic valley — a more relaxed way to enjoy the river and its gorges.

item.title: Tarutama Onsen — Guide
item.description: Tarutama Onsen is a secluded, old-fashioned hot-spring retreat tucked into the mountains of southern Kumamoto, offering a peaceful and nostalgic soak far from the crowds. Set beside a mountain stream amid deep forest, it’s known for its rustic, atmospheric open-air baths (rotenburo), where you can soak in warm mineral waters surrounded by the sounds and scenery of the valley — cool green in summer, coloured leaves in autumn, and a hushed, remote calm year-round.
